prior.altText: French press coffee pouring into a stable mug with grounds held below the lowered screen.
prior.prompt: Create a scientific-educational coffee brewing instruction illustration, one precise physical action/state, clear at 320px. Flat 2D editorial raster art with crisp dark espresso outlines, cream and pale blue and coffee brown solid fills, at most one flat shade plane. Genuine transparent background, landscape 4:3 composition with generous 12% transparent safe margin on every edge. No words, letters, numbers, logos, arrows, UI, decorative props, background island, photorealism, reflections or glossy 3D shading. Necessary equipment only. Keep anatomy mechanically accurate and stable. French press tilted safely by its black handle, lid seated and spout open. Mesh plunger lowered to grounds near bottom without compressing, rod straight. Smooth narrow coffee stream pours from small spout into stable ceramic mug; grounds remain in beaker, no overflow, hand on handle only, no loose lid falling, no force. Show full device and cup within margin.

replacement.altText: French press tilted by its handle so coffee reaches the open spout and pours into a stable mug, with grounds retained below the lowered screen.
replacement.prompt: Create a scientific-educational coffee brewing instruction illustration, one precise physical action/state, clear at 320px. Flat 2D editorial raster art with crisp dark espresso outlines, cream and pale blue and coffee brown solid fills, at most one flat shade plane. Genuine transparent background, landscape 4:3 composition with generous 12% transparent safe margin on every edge. No words, letters, numbers, logos, arrows, UI, decorative props, background island, photorealism, reflections or glossy 3D shading. Necessary equipment only. Keep anatomy mechanically accurate and stable. Create a physically accurate French-press DECANTING moment. One1liter French press with correctly seated secured lid, mesh plunger lowered to the grounds at the bottom, straight rod aligned with vessel axis. Tilt the whole press markedly about60degrees from upright toward a stable receiving mug on the LEFT; hand holds only its cool black HANDLE on the RIGHT. Show transparent glass so the remaining coffee is visible. CRITICAL FLUID PHYSICS: the remaining coffee's free surface is HORIZONTAL in the image/world, and visibly MEETS the actual OPEN SPOUT LIP at the lowest left edge of the tilted mouth. The liquid inside must connect continuously through the open spout to the narrow stream entering the mug. No air gap between internal coffee and spout, no stream leaving a dry area, no horizontal liquid surface below a high spout. Choose correct tilt and fill for the liquid to reach the lip. Grounds remain contained below the lowered mesh near bottom-right, no compressed puck. Receiving mug only partly full with generous headroom, no overflow. Focus single safe handle-held pouring action, no extra utensils, numbers, text, arrows or decorative background. Keep full press, handle-gripping hand and mug within transparent perimeter.

reason: Independent QC rejected disconnected pour: remaining coffee did not reach actual spout. Regenerated only this scene with physically connected free surface/spout/stream, correct tilt/fill and safe handle grip.
